Walthamstow Wetlands.extract: Walthamstow Wetlands is a 211-hectare nature reserve in Walthamstow, east London, adjacent to the River Lea in the London Borough of Waltham Forest. It is focused on the Walthamstow Reservoirs, built by the East London Waterworks Company between 1853 and 1904 as part of the Lee Valley Reservoir Chain. The site is one of the largest urban wetland nature reserves in Europe and is particularly important for wildlife due to its position within the Lee Valley. It serves as a byway for migrating, wintering and breeding birds. Visitors can freely access the site's natural, industrial and social heritage in one of the capital's most densely populated urban areas.

Tottenham Marshes.extract: The Tottenham Marshes are located at Tottenham in the London Borough of Haringey. The marshes cover over 100 acres (0.40 km2) and became part of the Lee Valley Park in 1972. The marsh is made up of three main areas: Clendish Marsh, Wild Marsh West and Wild Marsh East. The latter two are separated by the River Lea.

Lordship Recreation Ground.extract: Lordship Recreation Ground is a public park in Tottenham, London Borough of Haringey. It is over 20 hectares in size. Access is from Lordship Lane and from opposite Downhills Park in Downhills Park Road. It stretches approximately 750m north-south. The Moselle Brook runs through the park from west to east and the park also includes a small lake.

Tottenham Cemetery.extract: Tottenham Cemetery is a large burial ground in Tottenham in the London Borough of Haringey, in north London, England. It was opened in 1858 by the Tottenham Burial Board to replace the churchyard of All Hallows' Church, Tottenham which had closed the previous year. The original five-acre site was not entirely consecrated, with two acres designated for non-Church of England burials.

Downhills Park.extract: Downhills Park is a park in the West Green area of Haringey just on the edge of Wood Green and Tottenham.

Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.extract: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in London, England. It is owned and operated by the Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur, replacing the club's previous ground, White Hart Lane. With a seating capacity of 62,850, it is the third largest football stadium in England and the largest club ground in London. It is also used for NFL International Series games. It features the world's first dividing, retractable synthetic turf pitch used for NFL games, concerts and other events.

Duke's Aldridge Academy.extract: Duke's Aldridge Academy is a co-educational secondary school in the Northumberland Park ward of Tottenham in the London Borough of Haringey, United Kingdom.

Haringey Sixth Form College.extract: Haringey Sixth Form College is a mixed-sex sixth form college located in the Tottenham area of the London Borough of Haringey, United Kingdom.

Bruce Castle.extract: Bruce Castle is a Grade I listed 16th-century manor house in Lordship Lane, Tottenham, London. It is named after the House of Bruce who formerly owned the land on which it is built. Believed to stand on the site of an earlier building, about which little is known, the current house is one of the oldest surviving English brick houses. It was remodelled in the 17th, 18th and 19th centuries.

St Paul's Church, Tottenham.extract: St Paul the Apostle is a church in the Church of England Diocese of London in Tottenham, London, England.

All Hallows' Church, Tottenham.extract: All Hallows is an Anglican church in Tottenham, North London. It is one of the oldest buildings in the London Borough of Haringey, having been built as All Saints' Church in the 12th century, then re-dedicated as All Hallows in the 15th century.

St Mary's Church, Tottenham.extract: St Mary's Church is a Church of England parish church on the south side of Lansdowne Road in Tottenham in north London.

St Benet Fink Church, Tottenham.extract: St Benet Fink, Tottenham, is an Anglican church in Tottenham, London.

Ferry Boat Inn, Walthamstow.extract: The Ferry Boat Inn is a public house situated on the east bank of the River Lea, on Ferry Lane, Walthamstow in the London Borough of Waltham Forest. The oldest parts of the building date from the early 18th century, and it is a Grade II listed building, first registered by the Municipal Borough of Walthamstow in 1951.

Brook Street Chapel.extract: Brook Street Chapel is a church building in Tottenham, North London. The building was constructed for use as a meeting place for local Christians affiliated with the Plymouth Brethren movement.

White Hart Lane railway station.extract: White Hart Lane is a station on the Weaver line of the London Overground, located in Tottenham in the London Borough of Haringey in North London. It is 7 miles 11 chains (11.5 km) from London Liverpool Street and is situated between Bruce Grove and Silver Street stations. It is in London fare zone 3. The station is close to Bruce Grove and the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the home ground of Tottenham Hotspur Football Club.

Bruce Grove railway station.extract: Bruce Grove is a station on the Weaver line of the London Overground, located in central Tottenham in the London Borough of Haringey, north London. It is 6 miles 28 chains (10.2 km) down the line from London Liverpool Street and is situated between Seven Sisters and White Hart Lane stations. Its three-letter station code is BCV and it is in London fare zone 3.

Northumberland Park railway station (Lon.extract: Northumberland Park railway station is on the Lea Valley line that forms part of the West Anglia Main Line, serving the ward of Northumberland Park in Tottenham, north London. It is 6 miles 73 chains (11.1 km) down the line from London Liverpool Street and is situated between Tottenham Hale and Meridian Water. Its three-letter station code is NUM and it is in London fare zone 3. It is one of the stations that can be used to access Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Tottenham Hale station.extract: Tottenham Hale is an interchange station located in Tottenham Hale, north London for London Underground and National Rail services. On the National Rail network it is on the Lea Valley Lines section of the West Anglia Main Line, 6 miles (9.7 km) from London Liverpool Street, and is served by Greater Anglia and Stansted Express. On the Underground it is on the Victoria line between Blackhorse Road and Seven Sisters.

London Academy of Excellence Tottenham.extract: The London Academy of Excellence Tottenham is an academically selective free school for pupils aged 16–19. The sixth-form academy was opened in September 2017 in the London borough of Haringey.

St Philip the Apostle, Tottenham.extract: St Philip the Apostle Church is a Church of England parish church in Tottenham, London, and part of the Diocese of London.
